newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE SHARES RALLY ON LOWER MONEY RATES.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE SHARES RALLY ON LOWER MONEY RATES.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares rallied in an active trade on Friday as local institutional investors deserted the money market after the key treasury bill rate dropped sharply.

"Money market rates are coming down, with the treasury bill rate having fallen to around 15 percent today. That's why the market is getting firm and we are beginning to see a lot of interest in almost all the counters," one broker said.

Money market dealers on Friday quoted the buying rate of the treasury bill -- a direction pointer for other rates -- at 15.44 percent after the weekly auction on Thursday, down from last week's 19.36 percent.
But they said most market players felt the treasury bill rate had come down too drastically at the auction, with some of them adding one institution could have made a mistake in its tender price.
On the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Friday, brokers said buyers were also showing renewed interest in the bourse as they were anticipating rains soon.
The key 57-stock industrial index rose 31.93 points to close at 7,934.03. But it lost 75.14 points on the week.
Among the day's winners, publishing group Zimpapers leapt 180 cents to 1,980, blue-chip conglomerate Delta gained 50 cents to 3,300 as did bankers Barclays and Finhold to 2,250 and 950 respectively.

Engineering firm Gullivers at 210, clothing retailer Truworths and tobacco group TSL at 600, all climbed 10 cents while five-cent gains were recorded in discount house DCZ and brick-maker and building firm Mash both to 180.
Minings were generally unchanged save for a five-cent gain in Falgold to 140. The mining index edged 2.39 points to 1,218.75 -- a loss of 12.14 points on the week.
